newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 droops under Budget worries.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 droops under Budget worries.

text.p: The FTSE 100 traded at session lows mid-morning on Friday, with the market depressed ahead of next Wednesday's Budget.
The index was 34.1 points down at 4,623.8 by 0929 GMT.
"We are not so much running up to the Budget but stumbling. The market is washed out," said one senior trader.

Weeks of speculation over the contents of the July 2 Budget has given share prices a turbulent ride. Today was no exception, with an article in the Financial Times suggesting a windfall tax on utilities would be a hefty five billion stg, the top of the expected range.
The FT also said Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown is resisting pressure to scrap the abolition of a corporate tax (ACT) break on dividends in next Wednesday's Budget.
"Brown seems to be trying to warn the market about the Budget and it's ignoring him," said a dealer.
Power and water shares, after leading the market higher on Thursday on a Daily Telegraph windfall tax forecast of three billion stg, recouped early losses.
But British Telecom, seen as the biggest single payer with a one-off charge of up to one billion stg, fell 7-1/2p to 448p.
